findings.summary: Vertical tab, form feed, bare CR, FS/GS/RS, NEL, LS, PS end a comment, so a clause hidden in a comment is read: a file minisat, cadical and kissat all call SATISFIABLE gets ok=True, even through strict=True.
A header line's tokens after the fourth are ignored, so `p cnf 1 0 1 0` silently loses a clause, even under strict=True; `pq cnf 1 1` is also read as a header.

Tokens are whatever int() and str.split() accept, in both parsers: `1_0` is variable 10, U+0663 is 3, U+0660 ends a clause, and U+00A0 separates literals or hides a line as a comment. All three reference solvers refuse these.
A second `p cnf` line replaces the first, so strict=True passes `p cnf 1 1 / 1 0 / p cnf 1 2 / -1 0`, whose first header disagrees with the clauses.
header_mismatch has gaps: a tautology's literals after the clash do not count, so strict depends on literal order, and CNF.copy() drops the field.
`%` ends the formula wherever it appears, and real clauses after it are dropped silently even under strict=True when the header agrees. Documented as a SATLIB tolerance.
parse_proof documents reading as drat-trim's fscanf(" %i "), but `010` is 10 here and 8 under %i, and `0x10` raises here and is 16 under %i.
The documented bound on proof literals counts the text's length, so a comment or trailing spaces flip `5000 0` from ValueError to a checked RAT step.

Not a parsing bug, found here. Deleting a clause that is a reason at the root leaves its implied value in place, so `-2 / 2 1` with proof `d 2 1 0, -1 0, 0` gets ok=True though x1=T, x2=F satisfies it. Every oracle flavour rejects. Both engines.
Not a parsing bug, found here. On a rejected step that repeats a literal, failed_clause is deduplicated by Python and not by native: (2,) against (2, 2).

not_checked: drat-trim itself: it is not on PATH, so parsing-7 rests on its documented fscanf format and a C fscanf(" %i ") run, not on drat-trim.
Binary DRAT: dratify documents text proofs only.
Non-str inputs to the parsers (bytes, None).
parse_dimacs_file decoding (errors='replace', universal newlines): only exercised by hand in parsing-1, not by this generator.
Inputs large enough to hit the header and literal bounds' floor of 2^20, beyond single over-limit values; memory and time limits are not measured.
The position of a single header relative to clauses is not judged; a header after clauses is accepted as a tolerance.
Deletion semantics: proofs with deletions are judged only by engine agreement, re-rendering invariance and ok=True => unsatisfiable. The deletion corner owns the rest; parsing-9 surfaced anyway.
cdclkit's use of these parsers, beyond noting that its CLI calls parse_dimacs_file.
